validityCheck.title: Missing SafeERC20 - relies on tokens that return false instead of reverting

checks.evidence: Finding relies on tokens returning false instead of reverting on transfer failure. sUSDS (the mentioned prime token) is a standard ERC-20 that reverts on failure. However, the protocol is generic and could be deployed with other tokens.

validityCheck.notes: The protocol is designed generically, but sUSDS is the only explicitly mentioned token (BalancerPooler NatSpec). sUSDS follows standard ERC-20 (reverts on failure). If the finding relies solely on non-standard return-false tokens, it trends toward INVALID. However, if it also covers legitimate revert scenarios or applies to standard tokens, it could be VALID. Marked BORDERLINE because the generic design could admit non-standard tokens, but C4 rules default non-standard token findings to INVALID.

validityCheck.title: No actualReceived > 0 check - defense-in-depth, closely tied to DEDUP-001

checks.evidence: Finding is described as 'defense-in-depth' and closely tied to DEDUP-001. Defense-in-depth findings without demonstrated exploit path are QA at best.

validityCheck.notes: Self-described as defense-in-depth. Under C4 rules, findings without a demonstrated vulnerability path are not HM-worthy. At best QA/Low.

validityCheck.title: FOT bonding curve divergence - explicitly relies on fee-on-transfer tokens

checks.evidence: Finding explicitly relies on fee-on-transfer tokens. The code has FOT-aware patterns (balance-before/after) and MockFOTToken in tests, suggesting FOT tokens ARE in scope by design.

validityCheck.notes: Normally FOT findings are INVALID per C4 rules. HOWEVER, this project explicitly handles FOT tokens: (1) comments in NFTMinter.sol line 179 say 'balance-before/after for FOT safety', (2) dispatchers reference 'FOT-adjusted amount', (3) MockFOTToken.sol exists in tests. This strongly suggests FOT tokens are explicitly in scope. If the finding demonstrates that the FOT handling is insufficient (bonding curve uses pre-fee price but post-fee amount is dispatched), it could be VALID despite the general C4 FOT exclusion. The exception applies when FOT is explicitly in scope.

validityCheck.title: BurnRecorder accounting divergence - relies on token burn behavior being non-standard

checks.evidence: Finding relies on non-standard burn behavior. BurnRecorder.burn() simply records what it is told to record. Burner.sol calls IBurnable.burn(amount) then records the same amount. If the token's burn function does something non-standard, that is a non-standard token issue.

validityCheck.notes: The BurnRecorder records whatever amount the Burner tells it. The Burner passes the FOT-adjusted amount from the minter. If the finding is about a token whose burn() function does not actually burn the full amount, that is a non-standard token assumption. INVALID under C4 rules.

validityCheck.title: Missing slippage protection (mint price front-running + BalancerPooler zero default)
validityCheck.notes: No invalid patterns detected. Mint price front-running is a legitimate MEV concern: the price grows after each mint (line 186 of NFTMinter.sol), and a user's transaction could be sandwiched to pay a higher price than expected. The BalancerPooler defaults minBptAmountOut to 0 when extraData is empty (line 48), which is a real slippage vulnerability. Both are standard DeFi concerns with no C4 exclusion.

validityCheck.title: Authorized burner can burn NFTs without holder consent - centralization risk

checks.evidence: The burn function (line 298-302) requires msg.sender to be an authorizedBurner, set by owner via setAuthorizedBurner(). This is an intentional design pattern - the owner chooses who can burn. The finding describes a centralization risk where a trusted role acts against user interest.

validityCheck.notes: This is a centralization risk / trusted admin finding. The owner explicitly authorizes burner addresses. Per C4 rules, findings that require trusted roles to act maliciously are INVALID. This is not privilege escalation - it is the intended authority of the authorized burner role. At best this is a QA/Low centralization observation (L-xx or C-xx).

validityCheck.title: Price growth truncation for small prices
validityCheck.notes: No invalid patterns detected. The price growth formula (line 186: price + (price * growthBasisPoints) / 10000) will truncate to zero when price * growthBasisPoints < 10000. For example, if price=99 and growthBasisPoints=100, the growth is 99*100/10000=0. This is a legitimate arithmetic issue in the core pricing mechanism, not a token assumption or admin issue.

validityCheck.title: Owner can set price to zero

checks.evidence: setPrice() (line 239-244) is onlyOwner. The owner setting price to zero is a reckless admin action. The function is intentionally unrestricted to give the owner full control.

validityCheck.notes: Owner can call setPrice(index, 0) to allow free minting. This requires the trusted owner to act recklessly. Per C4 rules, reckless admin mistakes are INVALID. The owner has full authority over pricing by design.
